grades.detail: found ['nobody tells you that the real reason startups die']
every clip ends on terminal punctuation

cases.output:
[1] The biggest mistake founders make is hiring for passion instead of…
The biggest mistake founders make is hiring for passion instead of proof of work. That single decision quietly destroys more companies than bad pricing ever will. Here is the thing about hiring, you cannot interview your way to certainty. You can only watch what someone has already shipped under pressure. So we started asking every candidate for one artifact and one failure story. The artifact shows craft and the story shows whether they can learn. Most people think the answer is more process, and that is exactly backwards. Process is what you add when you do not trust the people you hired.

[2] Nobody tells you that the real reason startups die is running out…
Nobody tells you that the real reason startups die is running out of time, not money. You can always raise more money, you cannot raise more months of your life. That framing changed how we plan every quarter after that conversation. We now ask what we would cut if we had half the time and the same ambition. The answer is usually the thing nobody wants to own, which is why it survives. Look at the roadmap and find the project with no clear owner and no clear metric. That project is not a priority, it is a hiding place for a decision. Kill it and watch how much faster the rest of the quarter moves.
